title: Handled Multi Highlight cases too with highlight scroll
summary: When a highlighted verse is scrolled out of view, the reader now shows a small round bubble at the top or bottom edge. The bubble has the highlight's colour, an arrow pointing toward the verse, and the verse number. Clicking or tapping it scrolls to that verse. Several bubbles sit in a row, overlapping like cards on a computer and spread apart on a phone.

links.label: Issue 1716: Show indicators for highlights that occur outside the viewport

setup.title: Open the preview build on a computer
setup.body: Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer for the first sections. Open the preview link at the top of this page. If the page still looks like the normal Seed Bible, do a hard refresh: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, or **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac. The app saves a copy of itself, so this happens often.

setup.title: Start clean
setup.body: A private or incognito window gives you a clean start with no old highlights. You don't need to sign in: highlights work without an account.

setup.title: How to highlight a verse
setup.body: Click or tap a verse to select it. A toolbar appears with **Highlight colors**. Pick a colour, and the verse gets a coloured background. To select several verses in a row, select the first one, then click the others. To remove a highlight, select the verse and choose **Clear highlight**.

setup.title: Make the window a normal size
setup.body: Use a window tall enough to show about 10–20 verses at once, so that most of a long chapter is off screen. The tests use **Psalm 119**, which has 176 verses.

sections.title: Bubbles for highlights you can't see
sections.intro: Uses your own highlights in Psalm 119.

tests.title: A highlight below the screen shows a bubble at the bottom
tests.why: This is the main feature. Note: the issue describes a bubble that appears briefly when someone *makes* a highlight and then turns into a dot at the side after 3–4 seconds. This version shows a bubble for every highlight that is off screen, and it stays. If you think it should fade, say so in your notes.
steps: Open **Psalm 119**.
Scroll down to verse 100 and highlight it **yellow**.
Scroll back up to the top of the chapter (verse 1).
Look at the bottom edge of the reader and wait about 10 seconds.
expected: A round yellow bubble sits at the bottom edge of the reader, centred.
It shows a **down arrow** and the number **100**.
It is still there after 10 seconds. It doesn't fade or turn into a dot.
There is no bubble at the top edge.

tests.title: Clicking a bubble scrolls to its verse
tests.before: You need the highlight on verse 100 from the previous test, and you should be at the top of Psalm 119.
steps: Click the yellow **100** bubble at the bottom of the reader.
expected: The page scrolls smoothly to verse 100, which ends up roughly in the middle of the screen.
Once verse 100 is on screen, the bubble disappears.

tests.title: A highlight above the screen shows a bubble at the top
steps: Scroll to the top of Psalm 119 and highlight verse 1 **green**.
Scroll down until verse 1 is completely out of view (for example, to verse 50).
expected: A round green bubble with an **up arrow** and the number **1** sits at the top edge of the reader.
The yellow **100** bubble is at the bottom edge at the same time.
Clicking the **1** bubble scrolls back up to verse 1, and that bubble disappears.

tests.title: A verse that is only partly on screen gets no bubble
steps: Slowly scroll so that verse 100 is half visible at the bottom edge of the reader.
expected: While any part of verse 100 is on screen, there is no **100** bubble.
The bubble appears again as soon as the verse is completely out of view.

tests.title: Neighbouring verses with the same colour share one bubble
steps: Highlight verses **150, 151 and 152** all in **blue**.
Scroll back up to about verse 60, so they are below the screen.
expected: There is one blue bubble labelled **150–152**, not three separate bubbles.
Clicking it scrolls to verse 150.

tests.title: Neighbouring verses with different colours get separate bubbles
steps: Highlight verse **153** in a different colour from verses 150–152 (for example **pink**).
Scroll back up to about verse 60.
expected: The blue **150–152** bubble and a separate pink **153** bubble both appear at the bottom edge.

sections.title: Many bubbles at once (computer)
sections.intro: Uses a mouse or trackpad on a computer.

setup.title: Add more highlights below
setup.body: In Psalm 119, also highlight verses **110, 120, 130, 140, 160 and 170**, each in a different colour from its neighbour. Then scroll up to about verse 60. With the earlier highlights, there should be about 8 bubbles at the bottom edge.

tests.title: Bubbles overlap like cards and spread apart on hover
steps: Look at the row of bubbles at the bottom edge without moving the mouse over it.
Move the mouse over the row.
expected: Before hovering, the bubbles overlap like a fanned deck of cards. Only the last one shows its full number.
When you hover, they spread apart so every number can be read.
When the mouse leaves the row, they overlap again.

tests.title: Each spread-out bubble jumps to its own verse
steps: Hover over the row so the bubbles spread out.
Click the **130** bubble.
expected: The page scrolls to verse 130, not to a neighbouring highlight.

tests.title: A row too wide for the reader can be scrolled sideways
tests.before: This only applies if the spread-out row is wider than the reader. Make the browser window narrow, or add more highlights below, until it is.
steps: Hover over the row so it spreads out and is wider than the reader.
Look for small arrow buttons at the row's ends.
Click the right arrow (**More highlights to the right**), then drag the row sideways with the mouse.
expected: An arrow shows only on a side that has more bubbles hidden: at the start there's a right arrow but no left arrow.
Clicking the arrow, or dragging, slides the row sideways.
Dragging the row does **not** jump to a verse when you let go.

tests.title: Bubbles work with the keyboard
tests.why: People who don't use a mouse need to reach the bubbles too.
steps: Press **Tab** repeatedly until one of the bubbles at the bottom edge has a focus outline.
Press **Enter**.
expected: The bubbles spread apart while one of them has focus.
Pressing Enter scrolls to that bubble's verse.

tests.title: Keyboard still works right after a drag
steps: Press on the row of bubbles, drag sideways, and let go of the mouse button **outside** the row.
Press **Tab** until a bubble has focus, then press **Enter**.
expected: Enter scrolls to the bubble's verse the first time. It isn't ignored.

setup.title: Open the preview on a phone
setup.body: Open the preview link on a phone or tablet (or a very narrow touch window). Highlight a few verses far down Psalm 119 in **different colours** (for example 100, 110, 120 and 130), then scroll back to the top.

tests.title: Bubbles sit apart on a touch screen and can each be tapped
tests.why: There's no hover on a phone, so the overlapping deck couldn't be spread open. On touch screens the bubbles now start spread out.
steps: Look at the row of bubbles at the bottom edge.
Tap the second bubble in the row.
expected: The bubbles sit side by side with a small gap, not overlapping, and every number can be read.
Tapping a bubble scrolls to that bubble's verse.

tests.title: Swiping up or down on the bubble row still scrolls the page
steps: Put your finger on the row of bubbles and swipe **up** (to scroll down the page).
expected: The chapter scrolls as normal. The swipe isn't blocked by the bubbles, and no verse jump happens.

tests.title: A long row can be swiped sideways
tests.before: Needs more bubbles than fit across the screen. Add more highlights below if needed.
steps: Swipe sideways along the row of bubbles.
expected: The row slides sideways to reveal more bubbles.
Lifting your finger after a sideways swipe doesn't jump to a verse.

tests.title: Turning off Show highlights hides your bubbles
steps: In Psalm 119 with some highlights off screen, open **Settings**.
Under **Scripture elements**, turn off **Show highlights**.
Go back to the reader.
expected: Your highlights are no longer painted on the verses, and none of their bubbles show.
Turning **Show highlights** back on brings both back.

tests.title: Bubbles are readable in dark mode
steps: Switch the theme to **Dark** in **Settings**.
Go back to Psalm 119 with highlights off screen.
expected: Each bubble's number and arrow can be read clearly against its colour.
The bubble colours match the colours painted on the verses.

tests.title: Switching chapters shows the right bubbles
tests.why: The reader reuses parts of the page between chapters. This checks that bubbles don't point at the wrong verse afterwards.
steps: Go to **Psalm 120** (no highlights there). Scroll up and down.
Highlight **Psalm 120 verse 5**. Go back to **Psalm 119**, highlight verse 5 too, and scroll to verse 3, so that verse 5 is just below the screen.
Make the window shorter if needed so that verse 5 is completely out of view.
Switch to Psalm 120 and back to Psalm 119 a few times, each time placing verse 5 just past the bottom edge.
expected: Psalm 120 shows no bubbles from Psalm 119's highlights.
Each time, a **5** bubble shows exactly when verse 5 is completely out of view, and disappears exactly when any of it scrolls into view.

tests.title: Removing a highlight removes its bubble
steps: Scroll so a highlighted verse is on screen and its neighbours' bubbles are visible.
Select a highlighted verse that has a bubble when off screen (for example verse 100), and choose **Clear highlight**.
Scroll away so verse 100 is off screen.
expected: No bubble for **100** appears.

sections.title: Shared session (optional, needs two browsers)
sections.intro: The issue was written for sessions: seeing when someone else highlights a verse you can't see.

setup.title: Start a shared session
setup.body: In browser A, open the share menu and choose **Start and share session**. A link to join is copied. Open that link in browser B (a different browser, or a private window). Both should be on the same chapter, for example **Psalm 119**.

tests.title: Someone else's highlight off screen shows a bubble for you
steps: In browser B, stay at the top of Psalm 119.
In browser A, scroll to verse 90 and highlight it.
expected: In browser B, a bubble with a down arrow and **90**, in the colour browser A used, appears at the bottom edge.
Clicking it in browser B scrolls to verse 90.

tests.title: A session highlight's bubble goes away when the highlight does
tests.why: Session highlights only last as long as the session's **Highlight for** setting.
steps: Keep browser B at the top of the chapter after the previous test.
Wait until the session highlight on verse 90 would have expired (see **Session settings** → **Highlight for**).
expected: When the highlight disappears from verse 90, its bubble in browser B disappears too.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Highlights still paint normally on verses
steps: Highlight a verse on screen in a preset colour, and another with **Add custom color**.
expected: Both verses get their coloured background as before.
No bubble shows for a verse that is on screen.

tests.title: The rest of the reader still scrolls and selects normally
steps: Scroll through a chapter with no highlights.
Select a few verses by click, and by dragging across text.
expected: No bubbles appear.
Selecting verses works as before, and clicking near the top or bottom edge selects the verse there.

notCovered: How exactly bubble positions are worked out and kept up to date while scrolling. This is covered by automated tests.
The move of shared screen-measuring code into its own file, which also affects the session participant markers at the side of the reader. There should be no visible difference.
Screen reader wording of each bubble (for example "Highlight below, verse 100. Show it"). Check with a screen reader if you have one.
